name: Nigeria
dish: Egusi soup: a thick soup made with ground melon seeds, leafy greens and meat or fish, eaten with pounded yam.
person: Chinua Achebe, whose novel Things Fall Apart (1958) is one of the most widely read African novels.
custom: Aso ebi: guests at a celebration wear matching fabric chosen by the hosts, to show unity.
fact: Nollywood, Nigeria's film industry, makes more films each year than Hollywood.
where: On the Gulf of Guinea, bordering Benin, Niger, Chad and Cameroon.
land: Rainforest and mangrove in the south, savannah in the middle, dry Sahel in the north. The Niger and Benue rivers meet at Lokoja.
government: A federal presidential republic with 36 states. It returned to civilian rule in 1999 after years of military government.
issue: Insecurity in the north, from Boko Haram to armed banditry, and an economy that still leans heavily on oil. Over half the population is under 20.

name: Senegal
dish: Thieboudienne: fish, rice and vegetables cooked in a tomato sauce, often called the national dish.
person: Ousmane Sembène, often called the father of African cinema.
custom: Teranga: the national idea of hospitality, where guests are welcomed and fed generously.
fact: Senegal's Lake Retba is naturally pink because of algae that thrive in its salty water.
where: The westernmost point of mainland Africa, wrapped around the small country of The Gambia.
land: Flat savannah and dry Sahel inland, with a long Atlantic coast and the Senegal River in the north.
government: A presidential republic. Senegal has never had a military coup, which is rare in the region.
issue: New offshore oil and gas could change the economy, while many young people still risk the sea crossing to Europe.

name: Morocco
dish: Tagine: slow-cooked stew named after the cone-shaped clay pot it is made in, often with lamb, prunes and almonds.
person: Leïla Slimani, who won France's top literary prize, the Prix Goncourt, in 2016.
custom: Mint tea is poured from a height to create foam, and refusing it can seem impolite.
fact: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, founded in 859 by a woman, Fatima al-Fihri, is often called the oldest continuously operating university.
where: Across the Strait of Gibraltar from Spain, with coasts on the Atlantic and the Mediterranean.
land: The Atlas Mountains run through the middle, with Sahara desert to the south.
government: A constitutional monarchy in which the king keeps real power over the army, religion and foreign policy.
issue: The status of Western Sahara, which Morocco controls and the Polisario Front wants independent.

name: Egypt
dish: Koshari: rice, lentils and pasta topped with spicy tomato sauce and crispy onions.
person: Naguib Mahfouz, the first Arabic-language writer to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
custom: Sham el-Nessim: a spring festival dating back to ancient Egypt, when families picnic and eat coloured eggs.
fact: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
where: The north-east corner of Africa, linked to Asia by the Sinai Peninsula and the Suez Canal.
land: Almost entirely desert. Around 95% of people live along the Nile valley and delta.
government: A presidential republic in which the army has strong influence.
issue: Water. Egypt depends on the Nile and opposes Ethiopia's huge new dam upstream. The population has passed 100 million.

name: Ethiopia
dish: Injera: a spongy sourdough flatbread made from teff, used to scoop up stews called wat.
person: Mulatu Astatke, the father of Ethio-jazz.
custom: The coffee ceremony: beans are roasted, ground and brewed by hand, and served in three rounds.
fact: Ethiopia uses its own calendar, which runs about seven to eight years behind the Gregorian one.
where: In the Horn of Africa, landlocked since Eritrea became independent in 1993.
land: High plateaus and mountains cut by the Great Rift Valley. The Blue Nile starts at Lake Tana.
government: A federal parliamentary republic with regions drawn largely along ethnic lines.
issue: Recovering from the 2020 to 2022 war in Tigray, and tensions between regions. It was never colonised, apart from an Italian occupation from 1936 to 1941.

name: Kenya
dish: Nyama choma: grilled meat, usually goat, shared with friends and served with kachumbari salad.
person: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o, who chose to write in Gĩkũyũ rather than English as a political act.
custom: Harambee, meaning 'let us all pull together', is a tradition of community fundraising.
fact: Wangari Maathai, founder of Kenya's Green Belt Movement, was the first African woman to win the Nobel Peace Prize.
where: On the Indian Ocean, straddling the equator, bordering Ethiopia, Somalia, Tanzania and Uganda.
land: Coast, savannah, the Great Rift Valley and highlands around Mount Kenya.
government: A presidential republic. A 2010 constitution created 47 county governments.
issue: The cost of living and taxes. In 2024, mostly young protesters organised online forced the government to drop a finance bill.

name: Tanzania
dish: Ugali with sukuma wiki: a stiff maize porridge with braised greens.
person: Abdulrazak Gurnah, Zanzibar-born Nobel laureate who writes about migration and colonialism.
custom: Greeting elders with 'Shikamoo', a respectful Swahili greeting.
fact: Mount Kilimanjaro is the tallest free-standing mountain in the world.
where: On the Indian Ocean, between Kenya and Mozambique, including the islands of Zanzibar.
land: Savannah, the Serengeti, Mount Kilimanjaro and Lakes Victoria, Tanganyika and Malawi on its borders.
government: A presidential republic formed in 1964 by the union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar.
issue: Balancing wildlife tourism and conservation with the land rights of Maasai communities.

name: South Africa
languages: Zulu, Xhosa, Afrikaans, English and more
dish: Bobotie: spiced minced meat baked with an egg topping, with roots in Cape Malay cooking.
person: Nadine Gordimer, Nobel laureate whose novels examined life under apartheid.
custom: A braai: an outdoor barbecue so central to life that Heritage Day is also nicknamed Braai Day.
fact: South Africa has twelve official languages, including South African Sign Language.
where: The southern tip of Africa, between the Atlantic and Indian Oceans.
land: A high central plateau, the Drakensberg mountains and long coastlines. Lesotho is completely surrounded by it.
government: A parliamentary republic. The president is elected by parliament, not directly by voters.
issue: Inequality, among the highest in the world, and high unemployment. In 2024 the ANC lost its majority for the first time since 1994 and formed a coalition.

name: Iran
dish: Ghormeh sabzi: a herb stew with kidney beans, dried limes and lamb, served with saffron rice.
person: Hafez, the fourteenth-century poet whose book many Iranians still open at random for guidance.
custom: Taarof: an elaborate etiquette of politeness where offers are refused several times before being accepted.
fact: Nowruz, Persian new year, falls on the spring equinox and has been celebrated for about 3,000 years.
where: Between the Caspian Sea and the Persian Gulf, bordering Iraq, Türkiye, Afghanistan and Pakistan.
land: A high plateau ringed by the Zagros and Alborz mountains, with two large deserts in the centre.
government: An Islamic republic. An elected president and parliament sit beneath an unelected Supreme Leader.
issue: Women's rights protests after the death of Mahsa Amini in 2022, and the long dispute over its nuclear programme and sanctions.

name: Lebanon
dish: Tabbouleh: a herb salad of parsley, mint, tomato and a little bulgur, dressed with lemon.
person: Khalil Gibran, author of The Prophet, one of the best-selling poetry books of all time.
custom: Mezze: many small shared plates, eaten slowly over long conversations.
fact: The cedar on Lebanon's flag is a tree mentioned many times in the Bible.
where: A narrow strip on the eastern Mediterranean, between Syria and Israel.
land: A coastal plain backed by two mountain ranges, with the fertile Beqaa Valley between them.
government: A parliamentary republic in which top jobs are shared between religious groups: the president is a Maronite Christian, the prime minister a Sunni Muslim and the speaker a Shia Muslim.
issue: Recovering from a 2019 financial collapse and the 2020 Beirut port explosion, and conflict along its southern border.

name: Türkiye
dish: Mantı: tiny dumplings filled with spiced meat, served with garlic yoghurt and chilli butter.
person: Orhan Pamuk, Nobel laureate whose novels explore Istanbul and the meeting of East and West.
custom: Offering tea, served in small tulip-shaped glasses, to almost every visitor or customer.
fact: Istanbul is one of very few cities that sits on two continents.
where: Mostly in Asia (Anatolia) with a small part in Europe, controlling the straits between the Black Sea and the Mediterranean.
land: Mountains and a central plateau, with long coasts on three seas.
government: A presidential republic since a 2017 referendum gave the president much more power.
issue: It hosts more refugees than any other country, mostly Syrians, and has struggled with very high inflation.

name: Georgia
dish: Khachapuri: bread filled with melted cheese, the Adjarian version shaped like a boat with an egg on top.
person: Niko Pirosmani, a self-taught painter of everyday Georgian life.
custom: The supra: a feast led by a toastmaster, the tamada, who gives long, heartfelt toasts.
fact: Georgia is one of the oldest wine-making regions in the world, with evidence going back about 8,000 years.
where: Between the Black Sea, Russia, Türkiye, Armenia and Azerbaijan.
land: The Greater Caucasus mountains in the north, subtropical coast in the west and wine country in the east.
government: A parliamentary republic.
issue: Being pulled between hopes of joining the EU and pressure from Russia, which occupies about a fifth of its territory.

name: India
dish: Masala dosa: a thin, crispy fermented rice pancake filled with spiced potato, from the south.
person: Rabindranath Tagore, poet and the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 1913.
custom: Removing shoes before entering a home or temple, as a sign of respect.
fact: India has 22 officially recognised languages in its constitution and hundreds more spoken.
where: Most of the Indian subcontinent, bordering Pakistan, China, Nepal and Bangladesh.
land: The Himalayas in the north, the Ganges plains, the Thar Desert and a long tropical coast. Life follows the monsoon.
government: A federal parliamentary republic and the world's largest democracy, with nearly a billion voters.
issue: Debates over secularism and Hindu nationalism, and how to share the gains of fast economic growth. It became the most populous country in 2023.

name: Japan
dish: Okonomiyaki: a savoury cabbage pancake cooked on a hotplate, especially loved in Osaka and Hiroshima.
person: Haruki Murakami, whose dreamlike novels such as Norwegian Wood are read all over the world.
custom: Omiyage: bringing back small local gifts, often sweets, for colleagues and family after a trip.
fact: Japan has more than 6,800 islands, though most people live on the four largest.
where: An island chain in the Pacific, east of Korea and China.
land: About three quarters mountains, with many volcanoes and frequent earthquakes. Most people live on narrow coastal plains.
government: A constitutional monarchy. The emperor is a symbol; the prime minister and parliament (the Diet) govern.
issue: An ageing, shrinking population and how far to open up to immigration.

name: South Korea
dish: Bibimbap: rice topped with vegetables, egg, meat and gochujang chilli paste, mixed just before eating.
person: Han Kang, author of The Vegetarian and the first Korean to win the Nobel Prize in Literature, in 2024.
custom: Using both hands, or supporting your right arm with your left, when giving something to an elder.
fact: The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was invented on purpose in the fifteenth century so ordinary people could learn to read.
where: The southern half of the Korean Peninsula, divided from North Korea since 1945.
land: Mostly hills and mountains, with long coastlines and thousands of islands.
government: A presidential republic. It became a full democracy in 1987 after decades of military rule.
issue: The world's lowest birth rate, and the long stand-off with North Korea.

name: Vietnam
dish: Phở: a fragrant noodle soup with beef or chicken, star anise and fresh herbs.
person: Bảo Ninh, whose novel The Sorrow of War told the Vietnam War from a North Vietnamese soldier's view.
custom: Tết, the lunar new year, when people clean their homes and visit family to start the year fresh.
fact: Hạ Long Bay has around 1,600 limestone islands and islets.
where: A long S-shape along the South China Sea, bordering China, Laos and Cambodia.
land: The Red River delta in the north, the Mekong delta in the south and mountains in between.
government: A one-party socialist republic led by the Communist Party.
issue: Rapid economic growth under one-party rule, and disputes with China over islands in the South China Sea.

name: Indonesia
dish: Rendang: beef slow-cooked in coconut milk and spices until almost dry, from West Sumatra.
person: Pramoedya Ananta Toer, who composed much of his Buru Quartet while held as a political prisoner.
custom: Gotong royong: the idea of mutual help, where neighbours work together on shared tasks.
fact: Indonesia is made up of more than 17,000 islands.
where: More than 17,000 islands stretching between the Indian and Pacific Oceans.
land: Volcanic islands, rainforest and coral reefs. It sits on the Pacific 'Ring of Fire'.
government: A presidential republic and the third-largest democracy in the world. It has the largest Muslim population of any country.
issue: Moving its capital from sinking, crowded Jakarta to a new city, Nusantara, on Borneo.

name: Portugal
dish: Bacalhau à Brás: salt cod with shredded potato, onion and egg. The Portuguese say there are hundreds of ways to cook cod.
person: Fernando Pessoa, who wrote under dozens of invented personas, each with its own style.
custom: Fado: mournful songs about longing, tied to the feeling of saudade.
fact: Portugal and England have the oldest alliance in the world still in force, dating from 1373.
where: The western edge of the Iberian Peninsula, on the Atlantic.
land: Green hills and rivers in the north, flatter plains and beaches in the south, plus the Azores and Madeira.
government: A semi-presidential republic. Democracy arrived with the peaceful Carnation Revolution of 1974.
issue: Housing costs pushed up by tourism and foreign buyers, and young people leaving for better pay.

name: Spain
dish: Tortilla española: a thick potato and egg omelette, with an endless debate over whether to add onion.
person: Federico García Lorca, poet and playwright killed in the Spanish Civil War.
custom: La sobremesa: staying at the table to talk long after a meal has finished.
fact: Spain has four co-official regional languages alongside Spanish, including Catalan and Basque.
where: Most of the Iberian Peninsula, plus the Balearic and Canary Islands.
land: A high central plateau, the Pyrenees in the north and Mediterranean coasts.
government: A parliamentary constitutional monarchy with powerful regional governments.
issue: The Catalan independence movement, which held an unofficial referendum in 2017.

name: Italy
dish: Cacio e pepe: Roman pasta made with just pecorino cheese, black pepper and pasta water.
person: Elena Ferrante, who writes under a pen name and has never revealed her identity.
custom: La passeggiata: an evening stroll through town, to see and be seen.
fact: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than almost any other country.
where: The boot-shaped peninsula in the Mediterranean, plus Sicily and Sardinia.
land: The Alps across the north, the Apennines down the spine and active volcanoes like Etna and Vesuvius.
government: A parliamentary republic since a 1946 referendum ended the monarchy.
issue: Migration across the Mediterranean, and a lasting economic gap between the richer north and poorer south.

name: Greece
dish: Spanakopita: a filo pastry pie filled with spinach and feta.
person: Nikos Kazantzakis, author of Zorba the Greek.
custom: Name days: celebrating the feast day of the saint you are named after, often more than your birthday.
fact: Greece has about 6,000 islands, though only around 200 are inhabited.
where: The southern tip of the Balkans, with thousands of islands in the Aegean and Ionian seas.
land: Mountainous mainland and islands, with a coastline longer than almost any other European country.
government: A parliamentary republic. The monarchy was abolished by referendum in 1974.
issue: Recovering from the debt crisis of the 2010s, when bailouts came with deep cuts.

name: Norway
dish: Fårikål: lamb and cabbage stewed with whole peppercorns, the unofficial national dish.
person: Edvard Munch, who painted The Scream.
custom: Friluftsliv, meaning 'open-air life': a deep cultural love of spending time outdoors in all weather.
fact: Norway has given London a Christmas tree for Trafalgar Square every year since 1947, as thanks for help in the Second World War.
where: The western side of the Scandinavian Peninsula, reaching far above the Arctic Circle.
land: Mountains and deep fjords carved by glaciers, with midnight sun in summer and polar night in winter.
government: A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system. It is not in the EU but trades closely with it.
issue: Its oil wealth, held in the world's largest sovereign wealth fund, against its climate goals.

name: Poland
dish: Pierogi: dumplings filled with potato and cheese, cabbage, meat or fruit.
person: Wisława Szymborska, Nobel laureate known for witty, clear-eyed poems.
custom: On Christmas Eve an empty place is laid at the table for an unexpected guest.
fact: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw and remains the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.
where: Central Europe, between Germany and Ukraine, with a Baltic coast.
land: Mostly flat plains, with the Carpathian and Sudeten mountains in the south.
government: A parliamentary republic with a directly elected president. It joined the EU in 2004.
issue: Disputes with the EU over courts and the rule of law, and its front-line role next to the war in Ukraine.

name: Mexico
dish: Mole poblano: a dark, rich sauce made from chillies, spices and a little chocolate, served over chicken.
person: Frida Kahlo, whose self-portraits mixed pain, politics and Mexican folk tradition.
custom: Día de Muertos: families build altars with marigolds, photos and favourite foods to welcome back the spirits of loved ones.
fact: Mexico City is built on the bed of a drained lake and is slowly sinking.
where: North America's southern part, between the USA and Guatemala and Belize.
land: Mountain ranges, a high central plateau, deserts in the north and rainforest in the south.
government: A federal presidential republic with 32 states. Presidents serve one six-year term.
issue: Cartel violence and security, and its relationship with the USA over trade and migration.

name: Colombia
dish: Ajiaco: a chicken and potato soup from Bogotá, flavoured with a herb called guascas.
person: Gabriel García Márquez, whose One Hundred Years of Solitude defined magical realism.
custom: Las velitas: on the night of 7 December, families light candles and lanterns to begin the Christmas season.
fact: Colombia has more bird species than any other country in the world.
where: The north-west corner of South America, with coasts on both the Caribbean and the Pacific.
land: The Andes split into three ranges, with Amazon rainforest and plains to the east.
government: A presidential republic.
issue: Making the 2016 peace deal with the FARC guerrillas work, and the cocaine trade.

name: Peru
dish: Ceviche: raw fish cured in lime juice with chilli and red onion.
person: Mario Vargas Llosa, Nobel laureate who wrote about power, politics and Peru.
custom: Pachamanca: cooking meat and vegetables underground on hot stones, honouring Mother Earth.
fact: Peru grows thousands of varieties of potato, and the potato was first domesticated in the Andes.
where: On South America's Pacific coast, between Ecuador, Brazil, Bolivia and Chile.
land: A desert coast, the high Andes, and Amazon rainforest covering over half the country.
government: A presidential republic.
issue: Political instability. Several recent presidents have been impeached, removed or jailed.

name: Brazil
dish: Feijoada: a slow-cooked black bean stew with pork, served with rice, greens and orange slices.
person: Clarice Lispector, whose strange, intense novels are now celebrated worldwide.
custom: Carnival: days of parades and music before Lent, with samba schools preparing all year.
fact: Brazil is home to more people of African descent than any country outside Africa.
where: The largest country in South America, bordering every South American country except Chile and Ecuador.
land: The Amazon basin in the north, highlands in the centre and south, and a long Atlantic coast.
government: A federal presidential republic.
issue: Protecting the Amazon from deforestation, and deep political division.

name: Argentina
dish: Asado: a long, social barbecue of beef and sausages cooked slowly over wood.
person: Jorge Luis Borges, whose short stories about labyrinths and infinite libraries influenced writers worldwide.
custom: Sharing mate: a herbal tea passed around a group from one cup and straw.
fact: Tango was born in the working-class neighbourhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the late 1800s.
where: The southern cone of South America, reaching down to Tierra del Fuego.
land: The Andes in the west, the flat Pampas grasslands and Patagonia in the south.
government: A federal presidential republic.
issue: Repeated cycles of high inflation, debt and economic crisis.

name: Cuba
dish: Ropa vieja, meaning 'old clothes': shredded beef in a tomato sauce with peppers.
person: Celia Cruz, the Queen of Salsa.
custom: Dominoes played in the street, often loudly and with great seriousness.
fact: Many classic American cars from the 1950s are still on Cuba's roads, kept going by inventive repairs.
where: The largest island in the Caribbean, about 150km south of Florida.
land: Mostly flat and rolling land with mountains in the south-east.
government: A one-party socialist state led by the Communist Party since the 1959 revolution.
issue: A deep economic crisis, mass emigration and the US embargo in place since the early 1960s.

name: Jamaica
dish: Ackee and saltfish: the national dish, with ackee fruit cooked with salt cod, onions and peppers.
person: Louise Bennett-Coverley, who championed Jamaican Patois as a language of poetry.
custom: Nine Night: a gathering of music, food and stories over the nights after someone dies.
fact: Jamaica was the first Caribbean country to send a bobsleigh team to the Winter Olympics, in 1988.
where: An island in the Caribbean Sea, south of Cuba.
land: Blue Mountains in the east, limestone hills and white-sand coasts.
government: A parliamentary democracy with King Charles as head of state, represented by a governor-general.
issue: Whether to remove the British monarch and become a republic, and calls for reparations for slavery.
